Subject: Discovery follow-up + quick econ questions

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and two asks so we can put together a clean proposal: 

Call highlights (short):
- NeuroScale is piloting a conversational search product for healthcare providers (PII-scrubbed telemetry).
- Current pilot volume: ~5M tokens/month. Expected growth to 25–35M tokens/mo within 6 months if initial signals hold.
- Primary models: mixing completions-heavy flows (60%) with dense retrieval / embed-based reranking (40%).

Two quick asks to tune pricing options: 
1) Can you confirm an approximate range for what you consider an acceptable $/1M tokens target for committed pricing? (You mentioned “sub-$100 / 1M” in call — any band you prefer?)
2) Can you share a rough 3–6 month token ramp (CSV ok) so we can model committed-use vs burst pricing?

What I’ll do next:
- Put together two pricing sketches: a 12-month committed-use plan with tiered breakpoints and a 24-month multi-year incentive with upfront credit.
- Include the startup program founder credit option (one-time credit + faster onboarding credits) as a separate line item so you can decide.

Attachments: I’ve included a blank usage template (neuroscale_usage_estimate.csv) — fill in monthly expected tokens and mix if possible.

Proposed next step: if it works, I’ll loop in Ben (SE) and Rishi (my manager) for a short pricing sign-off and then send a formal term sheet. Can we aim for a decision window by Oct 5?

Cheers,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 07:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery follow-up + quick econ questions (NeuroScale)

Quick technical POV: 
- Their split (60% generation / 40% embedding) maps to a higher per-token cost on average because generation dominates compute. But embeddings at scale are heavy too — we should model both separately.
- If they accept an FP16/INT8 quantized 13B variant for most generation paths + batching and prefix caching for retrieval flows, we can realistically drive ~20% token-cost reduction (conservative). SE needs to model latency SLOs — pushing quantization too far may affect tail latency.
- For the 24-month proposal: we should require a baseline telemetry signal (first 6 weeks usage) to enable the 20% usage-credit unlock (measurable via token-level billing + Optimize config adoption).

Ask for the SE work: give me the populated CSV (tokens by flow type + peak seq lengths). I’ll produce a quick cost model (spreadsheet) by EOD.

Ben
